sections.description_of_the_ingredients:
1. Gavjawan (Onosma bracteatum) 
 Gavjawan (Onosma bracteatum), commonly known as Gaozaban, is a renowned herb in Ayurveda and Unani medicine, valued for its cooling and soothing properties. It is primarily used to support respiratory health, offering relief in conditions like cough, sore throat, and bronchitis due to its expectorant and demulcent actions. As a natural cardiac tonic, it helps strengthen the heart and manage palpitations and mild hypertension. Its anti-inflammatory nature makes it effective in reducing internal heat and irritation, especially during febrile conditions. Gavjawan also calms the nervous system, helping to reduce stress, anxiety, and promote restful sleep. In addition, it is beneficial in urinary disorders by relieving burning sensations and promoting healthy urine flow. The herb is also known to support skin health by clearing heat-induced eruptions and enhancing complexion. Overall, Gavjawan serves as a multipurpose herb that aligns with the principles of holistic healing. 
 Method Of Preparation 

 Take 1 part of Gavjawan (Onosma bracteatum) and soak it in 10 parts of water. 
 Then the next day, transfer the mixture into an Arka Yantra and extract the Ark from it. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 This Distillate has a range of medicinal properties that make it a valuable herb in traditional Ayurvedic and Unani medicine. Below are its key medicinal properties along with their explanations: 
 1. Sheetala (Cooling) 
 Gavjawan has a natural cooling effect on the body and mind, which helps in pacifying aggravated Pitta dosha. This makes it beneficial in conditions of excessive heat, fever, skin eruptions, and burning sensations in the body. 
 2. Hridya (Cardiac Tonic) 
 It supports heart function by strengthening the heart muscles and improving circulation. Its calming effect helps reduce palpitations and manage mild hypertension, making it ideal for stress-related cardiac issues. 
 3. Medhya (Nervine Tonic) 
 Gavjawan nourishes the brain and nervous system. It helps reduce anxiety, mental fatigue, and emotional disturbances, promoting clarity, calmness, and restful sleep. 
 4. Shwasahara (Anti-asthmatic/Respiratory Supportive) 
 Although the focus is on nervine and cardiac health, Gavjawan also helps clear respiratory pathways, reduce cough, and ease breathing in case of mild respiratory congestion. 
 5. Jwarahara (Antipyretic) 
 It is used traditionally to reduce fever, especially those associated with Pitta imbalance. Its cooling and detoxifying actions help lower body temperature and support recovery. 
 6. Raktaprasadaka (Blood Purifier) 
 Gavjawan helps cleanse the blood, which in turn supports skin health and overall vitality. This property is useful in managing skin disorders and promoting a healthy complexion. 
 7. Mootrala (Diuretic) 
 It aids in the elimination of toxins through urine and is beneficial in relieving burning micturition or mild urinary tract irritations. 
 Impact On Dosha 

 Pitta pacifying 
 Vata Balancing

Rooted in classical Ayurvedic wisdom and referenced in Ayurveda Sar Sangrah, this herbal distillate made from Onosma bracteatum (Gavjawan) offers natural support for stress-induced cardiac and neurological conditions.
